title: Adaptive fill-factor tuning and eviction signalization for microbatch backpressure
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Problem: Under sustained high QPS with mixed short and long sequences, our continuous microbatching sometimes overfills GPU KV cache allocation for hot tenants. That causes sudden eviction storms and cascading latency spikes for other tenants. Current admission logic uses a blunt token-based headroom threshold which doesn't distinguish batch fill density or ongoing eviction rates. This ticket proposes an adaptive 'fill-factor' metric plus explicit eviction signalization to the microbatch admission controller so we can apply softer, proportional backpressure and avoid abrupt workload disruption.
proposal: 1) Compute per-tenant and per-model fill-factor = active_kv_bytes / kv_reservation_bytes, weighted by recent batch density (tokens per request). 2) Emit eviction_rate signal from KV manager: short rolling average of bytes_evicted/sec and evictions_per_batch. 3) Admission controller uses (fill-factor, eviction_rate, recent_latency_p99) to choose a soft throttle level (0-1) applied to probabilistic microbatch acceptance and synthetic token-cost inflation for long sequences. 4) When eviction_rate exceeds a configurable hysteresis threshold, start gradual degrade path: reduce accepted batch sizes, prioritize prefix cache hits, and preferentially shed low-utility requests (e.g., long-tail embedding recalcs). 5) Expose tuning knobs in Console: target_fill_factor, eviction_hysteresis_sec, soft_throttle_curve, tenant_priority_overrides.
design_notes: Avoid binary admission: use continuous [0..1] throttle to preserve graceful degradation
Tie fill-factor to active allocation rather than instantaneous snapshot to smooth bursts
Weight fill-factor by batch_density to avoid penalizing many short requests that have low KV impact
Eviction signal must be cheap to compute and safe for multi-threaded KV manager (use per-shard counters + aggregator)
Provide default safe parameters for hosted tier and a separate set for Dedicated customers
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces eviction storm frequency, smoother P99 latency, better multi-tenant fairness
Cons: added complexity across KV manager -> admission controller surface; more telemetry and dashboarding required
Potential risk: incorrect soft-throttle curve could increase tail latency for priority customers; require overrides
implementation_plan: Phase 1: KV manager: add per-tenant per-shard bytes_evicted counters and compute eviction_rate aggregator (2 engineers, 1 sprint)
Phase 2: Admission controller: add fill-factor ingestion and soft-throttle mapping; implement probabilistic accept with synthetic token inflation (2 engineers, 1 sprint)
Phase 3: Console/Feature flags: expose knobs + rollout gating per-tenant; add default heuristics for hosted/dedicated (1 engineer + 1 frontend)
Phase 4: Canary: enable for 5% of traffic on a low-variance region, monitor SLOs and eviction signals; iterate (ops + oncall)
Phase 5: Gradual rollout to 50% then 100% with rollback path and kill-switch
testing_plan: Unit tests for eviction counters and aggregator correctness
Integration tests: synthetic workload runner with mixed short/long sequences to validate fill-factor responsiveness
Chaos test: force KV pressure and validate soft-throttle smooths P99 vs baseline
Performance test: ensure CPU overhead of eviction signalization < 0.5% and memory overhead negligible
End-to-end regression tests for Dedicated customers with pinned allocations
metrics_and_alerts: Primary SLOs: P50/P95/P99 latency for text-generation routes (compare baseline)
Alert: eviction_rate sustained > hysteresis for > 30s AND p99 latency rising > 20% -> page oncall
Dashboard: eviction heatmap over time with correlate to throttle levels and tail latency
rollback_and_fallback: Feature flag driven. If we observe higher-than-baseline error rates or tail latency regressions after canary, flip kill-switch to disable soft-throttle and restore previous token accounting. Always keep eviction-based hard-fail path unchanged as last-resort protection.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction_rate signal visible in telemetry for every host and matches offline counters
Admission controller uses fill-factor + eviction_rate to compute throttle level and records decisions to tracing
Canary shows >=30% reduction in eviction spike amplitude and no >10% regression in p95 across canary tenants
Console exposes knobs and default values; ops runbook updated with thresholds and remediation steps
